title: Knowledge Check 3 - Lessons 11-15
description: Questions pooled from Lessons 11-15 - Consulting and Implementation Strategies. Pass with 80% or higher to move toward unlocking the cert prep exam.

questions.question: A team builds in a Developer sandbox but needs production-like data volumes for integration testing. Which sandbox type fits, and why?
options: Developer Pro, because metadata copies faster
Partial Copy, because it copies metadata plus template-sampled data with a 5 day refresh
Full, because it refreshes daily
A second Developer sandbox, because they are unlimited
questions.explanation: Partial Copy copies metadata plus sample data defined by a required sandbox template at a 5-day refresh, which delivers realistic volume without consuming the single Full sandbox.

questions.question: Which statement about change sets is correct?
options: They can move records as well as metadata
They can delete a component in the target org
They resolve dependencies automatically without adding them
They contain only metadata reachable through Setup and require a deployment connection between the orgs
questions.explanation: A change set carries Setup-accessible metadata only, requires a deployment connection with the right outbound and inbound permissions, and moves no records.

questions.question: A production deployment fails at the coverage gate. What is the correct fix?
options: Redeploy with NoTestRun, which is allowed for production
Deploy with the CLI ignore-errors flag
Add Apex tests that raise code coverage to at least 75 percent
Deploy during a maintenance window
questions.explanation: Production requires Apex tests to run in the target org with at least 75 percent coverage, and NoTestRun is not available for production deployments.

questions.question: A team must ship a repeatable, versioned internal Agentforce console to 12 orgs and keep a clean upgrade path. Which deployment path fits?
options: Change sets, uploaded from a single source org
Unlocked packages, versioned from source control
A managed package published on AppExchange
Data Loader, loading the console configuration as records
questions.explanation: Unlocked packages are versioned, source-controlled, metadata only, and installable across many orgs with an upgrade path, which is exactly the distribution pattern described.

questions.question: You must load 300,000 Contacts that relate to Accounts already in production, and the load may be rerun. What should you use?
options: Data Loader with an external ID upsert, after the parent Accounts exist
The Data Import Wizard, because it matches on name
An unlocked package that includes the data
A change set containing the Contact metadata
questions.explanation: Data Loader handles this volume, the external ID makes the upsert idempotent on a rerun, and loading after the parent Accounts exist satisfies the lookup order.

questions.question: A production deployment introduced a regression two days after go-live. What is the deployment reality?
options: Use the rollback button on the Deployment Status page
Refresh the Full sandbox to revert production
Redeploy the last known good package or change set from source control
Do nothing, because metadata deployments revert automatically on failure
questions.explanation: Metadata deployments have no rollback, so the recovery path is redeploying the last known good version from source control, which is why versioned paths matter.

questions.question: Users were granted the new Agentforce app a month ago and have opened it twice. What is your first diagnostic step?
options: Send a training satisfaction survey
Verify the permission set assignment and app visibility using Login As
Refresh the Full sandbox
Add more fields to the record page
questions.explanation: Access precedes adoption, so confirming the permission set assignment and what the user actually sees with Login As separates a missing grant from a genuine usage problem.

questions.question: Which measurement best identifies friction inside the AI agent itself?
options: The number of logins to the org
The number of records created in the month
The share of sessions escalated to a human and the topics behind them
The average page load time of the console
questions.explanation: Agent Analytics reports sessions, resolutions, and escalations, and the escalation topics point directly at the prompt, action, or data that needs work.

questions.question: What does the Setup Audit Trail give you during a post-implementation review?
options: A log of setup changes covering about the last 180 days
A live stream of every user click in the org
Full transcripts of every agent session
Event-level telemetry for all users without an add-on license
questions.explanation: The Setup Audit Trail records setup changes for roughly 180 days, which is why a review that spans longer than that must export the trail before the window rolls.

questions.question: A user holds a permission set that grants Modify All Data. You assign a more restrictive profile. What is the user's effective access?
options: The profile wins, because a profile is the baseline
The permission is removed, because the restrictive profile overrides it
The union applies, so the user keeps Modify All Data until the permission set is unassigned
Access depends on the user's login IP range
questions.explanation: Effective access is the union of the profile and every assigned permission set, and only a muting permission set inside a group subtracts, so the assignment must be removed.

questions.question: Why does the Agentforce agent user belong in the same access review as human employees?
options: Because agents bypass all sharing rules
Because the agent acts with the agent user's permissions, so over-privilege becomes an escalation path
Because agents cannot be assigned permission sets
Because agent access expires every 30 days
questions.explanation: The agent operates with its own identity and permissions, so an over-privileged agent user lets anyone who influences the agent influence what it can do.

questions.question: Three weeks after go-live the business asks for a new object and a new record page. What is the right response?
options: Build it immediately, because the 30-day hypercare window covers new requests
Deploy it in the weekly change set without testing
Decline it, because the implementation is closed
Log it, size it against the success metrics, and schedule it into the release cycle
questions.explanation: A new capability is scope with a cost, so it is logged, sized, and scheduled rather than rushed untested or refused, and the release cycle supplies the natural window.

questions.question: A client signs a fixed-price SOW with a locked scope and a hard regulatory go-live date. Which delivery method fits, and why?
options: A waterfall delivery, because the scope is fixed and the date is contractual
Pure Scrum, because the platform demands iteration
Kanban, because it removes the need for phase gates
Whatever method the vendor's template prefers, since the platform dictates the process
questions.explanation: Waterfall runs scope, schedule, and cost as fixed and survives where the date is contractual, which is exactly the trade-off the question sets up; Scrum fixes time and cost and lets scope flex, which breaks the locked scope.

questions.question: You need production-realistic data volumes for a performance test but cannot risk copying every production record into a test org. Which sandbox tier do you request?
options: Developer
Developer Pro
Partial Copy
Full Copy
questions.explanation: Partial Copy uses a sandbox template to pull a defined subset of production records into 5 GB of storage, which gives realistic volumes without a full copy; Full Copy mirrors everything but refreshes only every 29 days.

questions.question: UAT is finished and the client's business lead says the system looks good in the steering meeting. What makes that milestone contractually real?
options: A verbal thank-you recorded in the steering minutes
A signed acceptance document that references the acceptance criteria in the SOW
A green status report from the delivery lead
A successful cutover rehearsal
questions.explanation: Acceptance closes the phase only when it is documented and tied to the criteria the client already agreed to, so a signed acceptance document that references the SOW criteria is the gate; a green report is sentiment, not acceptance.
